body:
Global crypto markets closed Tuesday under modest pressure, with total market cap sitting at $2.83T after a 24h decline of 2.68% despite intraday bids keeping the headline number off its worst levels. Volume came in at $94.1B, a figure that looks respectable on the surface but is heavily skewed toward BTC and ETH, suggesting rotation rather than fresh risk appetite. The mood is best described as cautiously defensive: the Fear & Greed index slipped from 69 yesterday to 57 today, a meaningful single-session drop that tells you participants are pulling back from conviction longs even if they haven't flipped outright bearish. BTC dominance at 59.3% and ETH dominance at just 10.9% confirm the familiar flight-to-quality dynamic within crypto itself, with capital consolidating around the largest name while altcoins bleed.

BTC printed $83,616 on the session, posting a 24h gain of +1.31% that flatters the tape somewhat given the 7-day return of -3.51% still looming in the background. The hourly is barely negative at -0.15%, meaning the asset is essentially coasting into the close rather than driving. Volume at $32.06B is solid and suggests the bid is real, not hollow, but bulls need to defend this range convincingly before anyone gets excited about fresh upside. The weekly chart remains the problem: three and a half percent lower over 7 days with no clean catalyst for reversal yet visible. Watch whether BTC can hold the low $83,000s on any overnight Asia selling; a failure there reopens the mid-$70,000s conversation that the market has been trying hard to forget.

ETH at $2,522.1 is the quiet underperformer of the day, managing only a +0.16% 24h move while carrying a -7.90% 7-day loss that is materially worse than BTC's comparable figure, a divergence that matters. Volume at $14.99B is adequate but the 10.9% market dominance print is a red flag for anyone structurally long the ETH/BTC pair. The broader altcoin complex is in worse shape: UNI is the standout, up +2.31% on the day at $7.59, though even that comes against a -17.40% 7-day backdrop that puts the 24h move in grim perspective. SOL at $107.85 slid -0.67% on the day and -11.42% over 7 days, ADA at $0.237552 dropped -1.91% on the day, and AVAX at $10.36 was the worst large-cap performer at -3.13% for the session and -11.30% over the week. DOT at $1.2 fell -3.64% in 24 hours and is now approaching levels that have historically attracted bottom-fishers, though the -2.19% 7-day loss looks deceptively mild relative to peers. LINK at $13.04 managed a modest +0.33% on the day and was one of only 3 assets in the tracked universe to post 24h gains alongside BTC and UNI.

The macro picture is complicated by 3 simultaneous currents hitting the tape today. South Korean authorities blocked 27 foreign crypto exchanges including Bitmart and KuCoin, a blunt regulatory move that contributed to South Korean equities sliding on AI-related concerns per the CoinDesk headline, creating a cross-asset feedback loop in a market that trades crypto and tech equities in close correlation. On the opposite end of the regulatory spectrum, Russia's Sberbank secured approval to trade crypto ahead of a December launch, a signal that state-adjacent institutional infrastructure is expanding in sanctioned economies whether Western regulators like it or not. On the institutional side, Federated Hermes joining Wall Street's tokenization push with plans for first onchain fund shares reinforces the slow-burn narrative that traditional asset managers are building rails regardless of short-term price action. The Anthropic warning about AI worms spreading autonomously across devices, while not a direct crypto catalyst, is feeding a broader tech-risk sentiment that is not helping high-beta digital assets today.

Looking ahead, the South Korean exchange ban deserves monitoring for secondary contagion: if affected platforms are forced to liquidate user positions or restrict withdrawals, you could see additional vol selling pressure hit the tape in Asian hours. The Stacks STX 50% surge over 4 weeks per CoinDesk is a micro-catalyst worth tracking as a proxy for Bitcoin L2 enthusiasm; if that narrative broadens it could pull BTC-adjacent assets higher even if spot BTC remains range-bound. The Fear & Greed drop from 69 to 57 in a single session is the most important data point in today's brief: if it crosses below 50 into Fear territory tomorrow, expect systematic deleveraging to accelerate and the altcoin carnage to deepen materially. The bull case requires BTC to reclaim and hold above $85,000 on volume comparable to today's $32.06B or better, while ETH needs to stop bleeding relative to BTC before any rotation trade makes sense. Until those conditions are met, the default posture is tight stops and reduced size.
